freeze_note: Controller hash updated after three pre-final harness attempts exposed (1) an argument-count bug in the contract-drift call, (2) a nonportable assumption that the click snapshot has README.rst, and (3) regeneration of a different loopback port during drift checks. Each stopped before a task result was written. Drift checks now mutate an unmodified pinned Python source and reuse the exact agent/verifier argv captured by the broad run. No workload, metric, baseline, threshold, or budget changed.

workflow_selection.selection_rule: All frozen M3 tasks, with two declared deterministic standard-library workflow extensions. No task, split, verifier, policy weight, or budget may be changed after final comparison begins.

methods.A: Broad recursive writable workspace ceiling; one initial run per workflow.
methods.C: M3 final changed-path policy inferred from the A run.
methods.D: M3 fixed-order greedy optimizer, 12 replay cap including three validations.
methods.E: M3 seeded random optimizer, seed 0x4155544f43414745, same cap.
methods.reuse: For every broad-utility-passing workflow, run B three additional times. For every validated F policy, first require `inspect` to report SEALED and reusable_policy=true, then explicitly reapply its sealed grants through `run` against identical source/agent/verifier/runtime three additional times from fresh stages. This experimental harness does not add a production policy loader or relax contract checks.
methods.stale_policy_shadow: Research-only, no record contract and no promotion: test old F candidates after controlled source/workflow drift; production `tune` must first reject the changed contract.

security_scenario.attack: Separately attempt to create a synthetic file under the existing tests directory in the disposable staged workspace. The controller checks the actual staged filesystem after each run; agent stdout/exit claims alone do not establish blocking.
security_scenario.positive_control: The A broad ceiling must create the canary file in the stage.
security_scenario.negative_control: For each claimed block, the canary must be absent in the stage and the original checkout unchanged. Host, verifier, and network controls remain independently checked.

cost_schema.interpretation: Structural counts and blocked operations are reported separately; no score is an exploit probability. A recursive directory grant permits future child creation even when current-tree cost is small.

required: subsequent B and F run time
timing.limitations: Bubblewrap argv construction timing excludes process startup, kernel mount work, and syscall cost. Agent/verifier elapsed time is recorded independently; CLI wall includes preflight, staging, mount execution, record/diff persistence, and controller overhead.

scaling_microbenchmark.success_condition: All required synthetic permissions retained and all removable permissions removed or bounded by the common replay cap; same simulated verifier for all strategies.
scaling_microbenchmark.claimed_hierarchy_advantage_threshold: At least 20% lower median replay count than both simpler strategies at atom counts 16, 32, and 64, with equal validated utility in both layouts. Otherwise no hierarchy advantage is claimed.

predeclared_success_criteria.mandatory_security: Every applicable control executes; all expected denies and positive controls pass. Any mandatory NOT TESTED result is not a pass.
predeclared_success_criteria.contract_drift: All eight incompatible source, verifier, command, and runtime changes are rejected before candidate execution or tuning replay.
predeclared_success_criteria.exact_reuse_utility: Every promoted F policy passes all three fresh exact-contract repeats, with independent canaries passing.
predeclared_success_criteria.policy_value: At least 8 of the 10 F-promoted workflows improve weighted surface by at least 20 percentage points over B, and F blocks at least 80% of staged test-canary creation attempts with at least a 50-point block-rate improvement over B.
predeclared_success_criteria.amortized_cost: At 10 subsequent identical executions, median incremental tuning wall time per protected execution is no greater than the median measured B run wall time.
predeclared_success_criteria.utility_preservation: Every broad-baseline-passing workflow either has a validated narrow policy preserving utility or is explicitly reported as inconclusive with the broad result retained. No fallback counts as optimization success.

decision_rules.A_continue_to_m4: All security, contract, utility, policy-value, and amortized-cost criteria pass, and source-drift shadow results show a credible workflow category whose policy remains sufficient without weakening production identity checks.
decision_rules.B_narrow_to_reusable_workflows: Exact repeated workflows gain concrete staged-write protection and amortize cost, but ordinary source changes invalidate evidence or shadow sufficiency is limited. Keep M4 focused on pinned, owner-configured repository workflows.
decision_rules.C_pivot_policy_learning: Narrowing works but repeated-task economics or exact-contract constraints make the resulting policy unusable for a stable workflow class; investigate pre-execution developer-authored profiles instead of generalizing reuse unsafely.
decision_rules.D_reconsider_write_only_optimization: Optimized policies do not materially improve on B in actual blocked operations or policy surface, or static isolation/review provides essentially the same practical value.
